validity.recommendation: Decide whether P1899 is a genuine parallel/twin trunk line or a duplicate of P1898 'UBTG-1-Berri' (249 km); if not a separately documented second pipe, merge P1899 into P1898 (or fold both into a single UBTG-1 trunk-line record). Treat the UBTG km-post family (P1898-P1900, P1910-P1912) as GEM-internal GIS segmentation, not independently published pipelines.
validity.researcher_notes: P1899 'UBTG-1-Berri 2' (247 km; diameters 56,36,38,40,42 in; Saudi Aramco; Saudi Arabia; gas) is a near-identical twin of P1898 'UBTG-1-Berri' (249 km; SAME diameter set 56,36,38,40,42; same owner; same endpoints unspecified). The only difference is 2 km of length and the ' 2' suffix. UBTG = Uthmaniyah-Berri trunk gas line. The whole UBTG family in the roster is named by kilometer posts and waypoints ('UBTG-1-km0-UBTG-1-km56', 'UBTG-1-km56-AY-1 KP916', 'Hawiyah-UBTG-1-km0', 'AY-1 KP 943-Riyadh') -- coordinate-pair/waypoint labels characteristic of a digitized GIS/map route (theodora-style) chopped into segment rows, NOT real published pipeline names. EXISTENCE/SOURCING: the gem.wiki page for P1899 cites ONLY OPEC Annual Statistical Bulletins (ASB 2012 p.75, ASB 2013 p.79, ASB 2017 p.136) -- national aggregate statistics that do NOT contain segment-level data for a discrete 247 km 'Berri 2' line. I could find NO independent source naming or confirming a second/parallel UBTG-1-Berri pipeline distinct from P1898. Web searches surfaced only the GEM pages themselves plus generic Master Gas System material (Aramco, Saudipedia) and a DIFFERENT segment, 'UBTG-3' (152 km, Uthmaniyah->Juaymah/Berri, per NS Energy / Saudipedia Berri Gas Plant) -- which is not a 247 km line and not the same as either P1898 or P1899. CLASSIFICATION/ATTRIBUTION are not in doubt: this is part of Aramco's dry-gas Master Gas System feeding the Berri Gas Plant, Saudi-Aramco owned, in Saudi Arabia (Eastern Province), corroborated contextually by Saudipedia's Berri and Hawiyah gas-plant articles. But the SPEC values (247 km, the five-diameter set) and the very EXISTENCE of P1899 as an entity separate from P1898 rest entirely on GEM-internal/map-derived data with no independent confirmation. Recommend human review to merge or to document the twin-line basis before any green tier.

fills.researcher_notes: Fuel=Gas supported contextually: the UBTG (Uthmaniyah-Berri trunk gas) line feeds the Berri Gas Plant, part of Aramco's Master Gas System (dry gas), per Saudipedia's Berri Gas Plant article. Note this is general MGS/Berri context, not a source naming P1899 specifically.

Country=Saudi Arabia supported: Berri/Uthmaniyah gas-plant infrastructure is in Saudi Arabia's Eastern Province (Saudipedia). Endpoint cities remain unspecified in GEM and could not be independently fixed for the '2' line.

Could NOT independently corroborate 247 km. No published source confirms a discrete 247 km second UBTG-Berri line. The figure is suspiciously close to P1898's 249 km (same diameter set), reinforcing the duplicate concern. Left unfilled rather than cite a non-confirming source.

Could NOT independently corroborate the diameter set. Identical to P1898's diameter set, consistent with the two rows being the same physical asset (or a GIS-derived split). Aramco's MGS uses 56-in trunk lines generally, but no source ties this specific multi-diameter set to a 'Berri 2' pipeline. Left unfilled.

Owner=Saudi Aramco (100%) is well-supported: all MGS / Berri Gas Plant trunk gas infrastructure is Aramco-owned and operated (Saudipedia). Solid for the family even though no source names P1899 specifically.

summary: P1899 'UBTG-1-Berri 2' flagged duplicate/existence concern: near-identical twin of P1898 (247 vs 249 km, same diameters/owner/endpoints); only sources are aggregate OPEC bulletins; no independent confirmation of a separate Berri line. Gas/Aramco/Saudi context confirmed via Saudipedia; length and diameter UNRESOLVED.
